tasks.title: Oracle SEQUENCE to PostgreSQL IDENTITY
Oracle Trigger to PostgreSQL
Oracle View: ROWNUM/NVL/DECODE to PostgreSQL
tasks.prompt:
Convert this Oracle view to PostgreSQL 16. Replace ROWNUM with ROW_NUMBER() OVER() or LIMIT. Replace NVL with COALESCE. Replace DECODE with CASE WHEN. Replace TRUNC(date) with date_trunc or ::date cast. Return SQL only.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_active_orders AS
SELECT
  o.id,
  o.order_no,
  NVL(o.amount, 0) AS amount,
  DECODE(o.status, 'A', 'Active', 'C', 'Closed', 'Unknown') AS status_label,
  TRUNC(o.created_at) AS order_date,
  ROWNUM AS row_num
FROM orders o
WHERE o.status != 'D'
  AND ROWNUM <= 1000;

tasks.title: Oracle BULK COLLECT/FORALL to PostgreSQL
Python: Oracle→PG type mapping function
tasks.prompt:
Write a Python function oracle_to_pg_type(oracle_type: str, length: int = 0, precision: int = 0, scale: int = 0) -> str that maps Oracle data types to PostgreSQL types.
Rules: NUMBER(p,s>0) → NUMERIC(p,s), NUMBER(p,0) → BIGINT if p>9 else INTEGER, NUMBER without precision → NUMERIC, VARCHAR2/NVARCHAR2 → VARCHAR(n), CHAR/NCHAR → CHAR(n), DATE → TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE, TIMESTAMP → TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE, CLOB/NCLOB → TEXT, BLOB → BYTEA, RAW → BYTEA, FLOAT/BINARY_FLOAT/BINARY_DOUBLE → DOUBLE PRECISION, INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH → INTERVAL, INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND → INTERVAL.
Handle case-insensitive input. Return only the Python code.

tasks.title: Python: Oracle DDL extractor via oracledb
tasks.prompt:
Write a Python function get_table_columns(host: str, port: int, service: str, user: str, password: str, table_name: str) -> list[dict] that connects to Oracle using the oracledb library (NOT cx_Oracle) and queries ALL_TAB_COLUMNS to return column definitions as a list of dicts with keys: column_name, data_type, data_length, data_precision, data_scale, nullable.
Use a DSN connection string with oracledb.makedsn or oracledb.connect(dsn=...). Return only the Python code.

tasks.title: Python: Migration rowcount validator
tasks.prompt:
Write a Python function validate_rowcounts(oracle_conn, pg_conn, tables: list[str]) -> list[dict] that queries COUNT(*) for each table on both Oracle and PostgreSQL connections and returns a list of dicts with: table_name, oracle_count, pg_count, match (bool), diff (int).
Use parameterized queries with bind variables (Oracle: :1 or :table_name, PG: %s). Use oracledb style for Oracle. Return only the Python code.

tasks.title: Python: OracleToPgMigrator class
tasks.prompt:
Write a Python class OracleToPgMigrator with:
- __init__(self, oracle_conn, pg_conn) storing both connections
- transform_ddl(self, oracle_ddl: str) -> str  that uses regex (re module) to replace:
  NUMBER(p,s) → NUMERIC(p,s), VARCHAR2(n) → VARCHAR(n), DATE → TIMESTAMP,   SYSDATE → CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, NVL( → COALESCE(
- migrate_table(self, table_name: str, batch_size: int = 1000) -> dict  that copies rows from Oracle to PostgreSQL in batches and returns {table_name, rows_copied, errors: list}
Use type hints throughout. Return only the Python code.
